findings.issue_text: [BUG] The diff converts the forEach callback to async (`bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {`), so the awaited getCalendar/deleteEvent promises are fire-and-forget — forEach never awaits async callbacks. Calendar event deletion during reschedule races ahead of the rest of Reschedule(); rejections from getCalendar or deleteEvent become unhandled promise rejections and the deletions can silently fail while the reschedule reports success.

[BUG] Same async-in-forEach conversion (`bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {`): the awaits inside the callback are not awaited by forEach. wipe-my-cal reschedule deletes calendar/video events as unawaited side effects; failures are unhandled rejections and the flow continues before cleanup completes.

[BUG] `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {` makes the deleteEvent call inside an async callback unawaited by the surrounding handler. Cancelling a booking via the bookings router fires calendar deletions as detached promises; errors are swallowed as unhandled rejections and the handler responds before deletions finish.

[BUG] The recurring-booking branch still uses `.forEach(async (credential) => {` after this diff converted the callback to async, leaving the awaits unawaited — inconsistent with the sibling old-behaviour branch in the same diff which was correctly converted to a for loop (lines 465-471). For recurring bookings, calendar event updates/deletes run as detached promises; failures are unhandled rejections and cancellation proceeds before the remote calendars are updated.

[BUG] The diff changes every appStore entry from a namespace module to a `Promise<typeof module>` (e.g. `googlecalendar: import("./googlecalendar")`), changing the type of the exported `appStore` object, but only the call sites appearing in this diff were converted to `await appStore[...]` — every other consumer of appStore in the repository (app metadata lookups, getApps-style iteration, any `Object.entries(appStore)`/value enumeration) now receives a Promise instead of the module namespace. Any call site outside this diff that reads `appStore[key]` without awaiting (or iterates its values expecting module namespaces) gets a Promise where it previously got a module, breaking at runtime with 'lib' in Promise always false or TypeError on property access — the diff only guarantees correctness for the files it touched.

[ADVISORY] getCalendarCredentials now stores an unawaited Promise in each item's `calendar` field (`const calendar = getCalendar(credential); return ... [{ integration: app, credential, calendar }]`), pushing the await obligation onto every future consumer of this function. The next consumer of getCalendarCredentials that treats `item.calendar` as a Calendar (the pre-diff contract) gets a Promise instead; only getConnectedCalendars was updated to `await item.calendar`, so this is a latent type-level trap the diff bakes into a public helper's return shape.

[BUG] The forEach callback was made async but forEach does not await it, so `await getCalendar(...)` and the subsequent deleteEvent run as fire-and-forget promises inside reschedule.ts. Rescheduling a booking with vital deletes calendar events only eventually or not at all; any rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection (crash under strict unhandled-rejection configs), and the surrounding try/catch no longer catches calendar deletion errors.

[BUG] Same async-callback-in-forEach defect: `forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...)` makes the awaited getCalendar/deleteEvent unobserved by the enclosing try/catch. Calendar deletion during reschedule becomes fire-and-forget; failures are unhandled rejections instead of handled errors, and ordering guarantees (e.g., completion before response) are lost.

[BUG] In the reschedule mutation, `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...)` is not awaited, so the awaited dynamic import via getCalendar and deleteEvent are orphaned promises. A tRPC reschedule request can return success while the calendar event deletion has not run and may fail with an unhandled rejection; error surfaced to the client is wrong (silent success on failure).

[BUG] Recurring-booking cancellation still uses `credentials.forEach(async (credential) => ...)` with `await getCalendar(credential)` inside, so none of the per-credential calendar updates are awaited by the handler. Cancelling a recurring booking can respond before (or without completing) the calendar event updates; a failing dynamic import or deleteEvent becomes an unhandled rejection and the user's calendar keeps stale events with a 200 response.

[BUG] getCalendar now awaits a dynamic import with no error handling, and every rejected import (chunk load failure, module-level throw in an app package) propagates as a rejection to all call sites that previously received a synchronous warn-and-null. A single broken app module turns previously-tolerated 'not implemented' paths (getCachedResults busy-times, createEvent/updateEvent/deleteEvent, cancel booking) into hard rejections — e.g., availability lookups in getCachedResults fail via Promise.all, breaking free/busy for all calendars.

[BUG] getCalendarCredentials still calls `getCalendar(credential)` synchronously and places the returned Promise into `calendar`; only getConnectedCalendars was updated to await `item.calendar`, leaving any other consumer of getCalendarCredentials holding a Promise where a Calendar was expected. Any code path (outside this diff) that consumes the returned `calendar` from getCalendarCredentials now receives a Promise object; `calendar?` property access on a Promise yields undefined behavior rather than a calendar, silently breaking integration payloads.

[ADVISORY] Every appStore entry changed from a namespace import to an unevaluated dynamic-import Promise, silently changing the public contract of the default export for all consumers, including out-of-tree call sites that index appStore without awaiting. Any consumer not touched in this diff (e.g., other appStore[dirName] readers like stripe webhooks or getApps in apps/*) that reads `appStore[...]` synchronously now gets a Promise and the `'lib' in app` guard fails, degrading those integrations to 'not implemented'.

[ADVISORY] getVideoAdapters now sequentially awaits a dynamic import per credential inside a for-loop, serializing module resolution on every busy-times/createMeeting call instead of one parallel Promise.all. Users with multiple video credentials pay N sequential await round-trips on the availability hot path, adding latency to every booking-page load.

[ADVISORY] The old forEach path was correctly converted to a for-of loop with sequential awaits here, but identical forEach(async ...) sites in vital/reschedule.ts, wipemycalother/reschedule.ts, bookings.tsx, and the recurring-cancellation block above were not — the diff applies the correct pattern in only one of five affected sites. Reviewers and future maintainers see the correct conversion pattern in one file and can reasonably assume the pattern was applied uniformly; the four remaining broken sites are easy to miss in follow-up review.

[ADVISORY] getCachedResults awaits getCalendar for all credentials before computing busy times, converting a previously synchronous, non-failing calendar construction into an await whose single rejected import rejects the whole availability computation (Promise.all semantics downstream). Availability checking for a user gains a new total-failure mode tied to module loading; no test in the diff covers a rejected import on this path (diff contains no spec files under spec/, test/, or *.spec.*), so a regression here would silently break booking availability.

[BUG] The forEach callback was made async, so each iteration now returns a discarded promise instead of a value consumed by the loop body, converting previously synchronous delete calls into fire-and-forget promises. deleteEvent/deleteMeeting rejections escape the surrounding try/catch entirely (the callback's promise is never awaited), so a failing calendar deletion during reschedule is swallowed as an unhandled rejection while the reschedule reports success; before this diff the same failure was caught and handled.

[BUG] Same async-forEach conversion makes the per-reference deletion promises fire-and-forget and invisible to the enclosing try/catch. Calendar/video deletion errors during reschedule become unhandled rejections and the outer error handling that previously caught them no longer runs; deletions also race ahead of the reschedule completing.

[BUG] The reschedule handler's forEach callback was made async, discarding each returned promise instead of collecting them as the surrounding code expects. Calendar deleteEvent failures during booking reschedule become unhandled promise rejections outside the handler's error handling, and the router can respond before the deletions complete or fail, so clients see success while third-party events remain.

[BUG] The recurring-event credential forEach was converted to an async callback whose promises are never awaited. Per-credential calendar updateEvent calls for recurring bookings are no longer synchronized with the handler: failures surface as unhandled rejections and the cancel response can return before any of the recurring-event deletions have run.

[ADVISORY] getCalendarCredentials still calls the now-async getCalendar without await, so the `calendar` field it returns is a Promise, not a Calendar. Any consumer of getCalendarCredentials other than getConnectedCalendars (which happens to await item.calendar) receives a Promise where the type signature claims a Calendar — the type system no longer describes the data, and the next consumer will silently get a Promise and fail its `calendar` checks.

[ADVISORY] This hunk rewrites working synchronous iteration into a for-of with sequential awaits, which is behavior drift (parallelism lost) bundled into a lazy-import refactor. Calendar deletions in the legacy path now run serially instead of concurrently, adding latency to every legacy-booking cancellation proportional to the number of calendar credentials — a performance regression unrelated to making imports async, untraceable to any stated requirement.

[ADVISORY] Every appStore entry is now a top-level Promise created eagerly at module load, so all 29 app modules are still loaded/instantiated at startup (just as microtasks), negating the code-splitting benefit the change implies. The lazy-import pattern gives no deferred loading: bundlers will still include every app chunk and the module graph kicks off all 29 imports on first touch of appStore; any real deferral (and bundle-size win) requires making appStore a map of thunks or dynamic import by name, so the current shape encodes the wrong invariant for future apps.

[BUG] bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...) fire-and-forgets the async callback, so the awaited getCalendar/deleteEvent work runs outside any awaited promise chain Reschedule returns success to the caller before the calendar/video deletions complete or fail; a rejected deleteEvent becomes an unhandled promise rejection and the external calendar event is silently left behind on the rescheduled booking

[BUG] Same forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...) pattern: the async deletion work is not awaited or collected into Promise.all wipe-my-cal reschedule completes with deletions still in flight; failures are unhandled rejections and stale external events persist

[BUG] bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...) in the editLocation/reschedule mutation never awaits the async callback The tRPC mutation resolves before calendar event deletion finishes; errors from getCalendar/deleteEvent surface as unhandled rejections instead of mutation errors, so users see success while the old calendar event remains

[BUG] The forEach(async (credential) => ...) over calendar credentials was already async-callback based, but this diff adds an await inside it, deepening the fire-and-forget chain with no collection of the promises Recurring-booking calendar updates run unawaited; handler success is returned while updates may still be failing with unhandled rejections, leaving recurring external events out of sync with the DB

[BUG] getCalendarCredentials still builds the {integration, credential, calendar} tuple by calling the now-async getCalendar synchronously, embedding a Promise in item.calendar and relying on the single downstream consumer (getConnectedCalendars) to await it Any other consumer of getCalendarCredentials (or the exported tuple shape) that reads item.calendar as a Calendar gets a Promise — truthy even when the calendar is null, defeating the `if (!calendar)` guard and leaking a broken 'connected' calendar entry; the contract change is only patched at one call site

[ADVISORY] getVideoAdapters now awaits the dynamic import sequentially inside a for-loop, serializing N module loads that the previous synchronous reduce performed for free Every getBusyVideoTimes/createMeeting call pays N sequential awaited import resolutions (even if module-cache hits, each is an await tick); on a busy-time hot path across many credentials this adds latency linearly — batching with Promise.all over the appStore lookups would restore parallelism

[ADVISORY] The old-behaviour branch was correctly rewritten to a sequential for-loop awaiting getCalendar per credential, while sibling code in the same file (line 458) kept the forEach-async shape — two divergent patterns for the same operation now coexist The next editor copying the nearby forEach pattern propagates the fire-and-forget bug; the fix pattern proven correct in this same diff is not applied to the adjacent identical case

[BUG] Converting the forEach callback to async makes every deleteEvent/deleteMeeting call fire-and-forget, so Reschedule resolves before (and independently of) the calendar/video deletions. On reschedule of a vital booking, the handler completes while deletions are still in flight; any rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection and the old event can silently remain live in the external calendar.

[BUG] Same async-forget forEach: the callback now returns a Promise that forEach discards, so the deletions are neither awaited nor error-handled. wipemycalother reschedule can leave stale events in the external calendar and swallow deletion errors as unhandled rejections.

[BUG] The reschedule mutation's forEach callback is now async, so calendar deleteEvent calls are fire-and-forget and the mutation returns success before/independently of them. A user rescheduling via the bookings router gets a success response while the old calendar event deletion may have failed with an unhandled rejection; data silently diverges between Cal.com and the external calendar.

[BUG] The forEach over calendar credentials was made async without converting the loop to awaited iteration, so the per-credential updateEvent/deleteEvent work is unawaited inside the cancel handler. Cancellation of recurring-event bookings proceeds and persists booking state before the external calendar updates resolve; failures surface only as unhandled promise rejections.

[ADVISORY] The dynamic-import refactor does not actually defer loading: every import() promise is created eagerly at module evaluation, so all app modules still load at startup and the only real change is that every consumer had to become async. The stated intent (async/lazy import of appStore packages) is not achieved — bundle and startup behavior are effectively unchanged while ~20 call sites were churned to async, so the diff pays the full migration cost for no benefit; a reviewer or future reader assuming lazy loading will be misled.

[ADVISORY] appStore values changed from module objects to Promises, silently changing the public contract of the exported default for any consumer not updated in this diff. Any remaining synchronous reader of appStore (e.g. app metadata/listing code outside this diff) now receives a Promise object, which is truthy and lacks lib/keys, producing wrong behavior or silent no-ops instead of a compile error.

[ADVISORY] getCalendarCredentials still calls getCalendar synchronously, so the returned `calendar` field is now a Promise, not a Calendar, and only getConnectedCalendars in this diff was adapted to await it. In the appStore variant === 'calendar' path, any other consumer of getCalendarCredentials output receives an always-truthy Promise where the old code returned a usable Calendar or null, so `calendar`-truthiness checks elsewhere silently pass with a Promise and then fail on use.

[ADVISORY] getCachedResults now eagerly instantiates every calendar adapter via Promise.all(getCalendar(...)) before the busy-times fetch, whereas getCalendar construction was previously free. Every availability check pays the async module-resolution cost for all calendar credentials up front, adding latency to the hot availability path per user request.

[ADVISORY] getVideoAdapters was rewritten from a reduce to a sequential for-loop with per-credential await, serializing dynamic-import resolution that the old synchronous code did not pay per call. Each call to createMeeting/updateMeeting/deleteMeeting re-resolves the module import and awaits it serially, adding per-booking latency on booking-critical paths.

[ADVISORY] Module-load failures move from startup (static import) to first-use (await appStore[key]), turning deterministic boot-time errors into per-request runtime failures. A broken app package now fails only when a user with that credential triggers booking/cancellation, surfacing as request-level errors instead of a caught-at-deploy startup failure.

[BUG] The forEach callback was made async but forEach does not await promises, so the calendar deleteEvent and video deleteMeeting calls inside it become fire-and-forget and their rejections are unhandled. During reschedule/cancel, external calendar/video deletions are no longer awaited or error-checked: a failing deletion is silently dropped from the request outcome (user is told the reschedule succeeded while the external event still exists), and an awaited rejection inside the callback becomes an unhandled promise rejection that can crash the Node process.

[BUG] forEach with an async callback means the awaited getCalendar/deleteEvent work inside the callback is not awaited by Reschedule, so the returned promises are discarded. Calendar event deletions during reschedule proceed without any error propagation: failures are invisible to the caller and an unhandled rejection from the dynamic import inside getCalendar can take down the worker process.

[BUG] Same async-callback-in-forEach defect: the awaited calendar deletion promises inside the forEach body are not collected or awaited. Deletion failures during reschedule are silently swallowed and any rejection escapes as an unhandled promise rejection instead of surfacing to the reschedule error path.

[BUG] The forEach(async (credential) => ...) wraps awaited calendar deletions in a callback whose promises are never awaited, so the recurring-event deletion loop is fire-and-forget. For recurring bookings, per-credential calendar event deletions run detached from handler control flow: partial deletion failures are unreported (calendar stays populated despite booking cancellation) and rejections surface as unhandled promise rejections rather than the handler's error response.

[ADVISORY] getCalendarCredentials still assigns the now-async getCalendar(credential) result synchronously, so each returned item's calendar field is a Promise, and only the getConnectedCalendars call site in this diff was updated to await it. Any other existing consumer of getCalendarCredentials (outside this diff) now receives Promise objects where it previously received Calendar instances; calling calendar methods on it throws, and the mixed sync/async contract forces every future call site to remember the double-await (await item.calendar).

[BUG] forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...) fires the now-async getCalendar/deleteEvent work as unawaited floating promises, so Reschedule resolves before any calendar deletion starts. Cancellation of a booking returns success while calendar event deletion runs unsupervised; any rejection inside the callback is unhandled (unhandled promise rejection / silent data leak where the remote calendar event is never deleted and no error surfaces to the caller).

[BUG] Same forEach(async ...) fire-and-forget conversion: async callback makes the awaited getCalendar call a floating promise that forEach ignores. Reschedule completes before remote deletions run; failures inside the callback become unhandled rejections and deleted calendar events are silently lost.

[BUG] Converting forEach callback to async makes the awaited getCalendar(...).deleteEvent(...) chain an unawaited floating promise inside the tRPC reschedule mutation. The mutation responds before calendar deletions execute; a failed deletion is swallowed as an unhandled rejection, leaving stale events on the user's calendar with no error reported.

[BUG] The .forEach(async (credential) => {...}) containing the awaited getCalendar loop floats every promise: the surrounding handler never awaits these updates. handleCancelBooking finishes while per-credential calendar updates are still in flight; errors in updateEvent are unhandled rejections and recurring-event calendar cleanup can be silently skipped.

[ADVISORY] getCalendarCredentials now stores a Promise<Calendar|null> in item.calendar with no comment or type change, so every consumer must know to await it — an implicit contract change on the returned shape. The next consumer of calendarCredentials that treats item.calendar as a Calendar (as all callers did before this diff) gets a truthy Promise where a null check was expected, bypassing the `if (!calendar)` guard in getConnectedCalendars-style logic; only consumers updated in this diff await it.

[BUG] forEach callback made async so the calendar deleteEvent promise is fire-and-forget: the surrounding try/catch no longer observes failures and the reschedule handler completes before any external calendar event deletion runs or errors. On reschedule, deletion of the old external calendar event silently fails or is never awaited; stale calendar events accumulate and errors are unlogged/unhandled — silent data inconsistency for users of the vital app's reschedule flow.

[BUG] Same async-callback-in-forEach defect: the awaited getCalendar/deleteEvent inside the async forEach callback is detached from the enclosing async function, so failures in calendar deletion are unobservable and the handler returns before deletes finish. wipemycalother reschedule leaves old external calendar events undeleted when the async delete rejects or is still pending at process exit; previously synchronous error propagation is lost.

[BUG] bookingRefsFiltered.forEach callback converted to async, orphaning the calendar deleteEvent promise: the mutation handler resolves while deletions are in-flight and rejections become unhandledRejection. Rescheduling a booking via the tRPC endpoint can leave the old external calendar event in place (data not cleaned up) and surface unhandled promise rejections in the API server instead of the mutation's error path.

[BUG] getCalendarCredentials still calls the now-async getCalendar(credential) without await, so `calendar` is a Promise — always truthy — and the `calendar` field handed to getConnectedCalendars (which awaits item.calendar) is a resolved Promise-wrapped calendar only if the inner shape matches; for the non-calendar variant path the null-check semantics change from 'unimplemented app returns null' to 'unimplemented app returns a Promise'. Apps whose lib lacks CalendarService no longer yield a falsy calendar at this call site; downstream consumers that don't await (any call site of getCalendarCredentials not updated in this diff) receive a Promise where they previously received Calendar|null, producing runtime errors like 'calendar.getAvailability is not a function' when rendering connected calendars.

[ADVISORY] getCachedResults resolves all calendars with Promise.all before mapping, but the map in getCalendarCredentials (line 28-31) does not, leaving the codebase with two different conventions for the same async getCalendar return value in adjacent functions. The next caller to copy either pattern has a 50% chance of copying the broken one; the mixed sync/async usage is the standing source of the Promise-as-value bugs introduced in this diff.

[BUG] The recurring-bookings forEach callback is made async (await getCalendar inside callback), so the per-credential delete/update loop is fire-and-forget and its errors are no longer caught by any enclosing handler. Cancellation of a recurring booking can silently skip deleting/updating some calendar credentials' external events when the dynamic import or deleteEvent rejects; affected users keep orphaned calendar events with no error surfaced to the API response.

[BUG] forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...) with an awaited getCalendar inside makes the deletion work fire-and-forget and moves it outside the enclosing try/catch, so calendar/video deletion failures during reschedule are unhandled rejections invisible to the caller. A failing deleteEvent (e.g. network error to Google/Zoom) rejects the async callback's promise which nothing awaits; the outer try/catch no longer sees it, reschedule reports success while the old event stays live on the provider's calendar.

[BUG] Same forEach(async ...) pattern: the awaited getCalendar/deleteEvent work is unawaited and any rejection is swallowed as an unhandled promise rejection, escaping the surrounding try/catch. WipeMyCal reschedule silently drops event deletion failures; the API response still reports success.

[BUG] bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ...) is not awaited, so the calendar deleteEvent calls kicked off inside the async callback are fire-and-forget and their rejections are never observed by the tRPC handler. During a tRPC reschedule/cancel, a failing calendar deleteEvent rejects unobserved while the mutation returns success to the client; the stale remote event persists with no error surfaced.

[BUG] user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => ...) is unawaited, so the awaited getCalendar and the updateEvent/delete calls inside run fire-and-forget with no rejection handler. Recurring-booking cancellation updates to other calendar instances can fail silently (unhandled rejection); handleCancelBooking completes and reports success while remote events remain booked.

[BUG] getCalendar now awaits a dynamic import whose rejection propagates to every caller, but several call sites in this diff invoke it inside unguarded .map/.forEach bodies, converting a previously sync-safe null return into an unhandled rejection that aborts the whole operation. If one app module fails to load (build chunk error or module top-level throw), getCachedResults' Promise.all rejects and busy-time fetching for ALL calendars fails, and CalendarManager.getCalendarCredentials' getCalendar(credential) at line 28 produces an unawaited rejected promise — previously a bad app only logged a warning and returned null.

[ADVISORY] getCalendarCredentials still calls the now-async getCalendar synchronously and stores the resulting Promise in item.calendar, leaving only the getConnectedCalendars caller aware that it must await; every other consumer of this function's shape silently receives a Promise where it used to receive Calendar | null. Any caller (in-tree or out-of-tree) that reads item.calendar without awaiting gets a always-truthy Promise, passing the `if (!calendar)` null guard and then operating on a Promise object; the type of the returned array was not updated in this diff to reflect that.

[ADVISORY] The sequential for-loop awaiting getCalendar per credential serializes dynamic imports that could run concurrently, a hot-path latency regression on the cancel-booking request. For users with multiple calendar credentials, cancel-booking latency grows linearly with credential count where the previous code (and a Promise.all) issued them concurrently.

goldens.comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
